claims.title: Finite Dobrushin total-variation contraction
claims.scope: two finite input probability distributions passed through one common finite row-stochastic outcome channel
assumptions: the same record-independent channel is applied under both compared input laws
distance is measured in total variation
nonclaims: a record-dependent intervention channel can insert new record information and is outside this theorem
the coefficient is not asserted to contract every statistical divergence by the same factor

claims.title: Query-specific predictive-law channel contraction
claims.scope: a finite stochastic future-query family with one common post-processing channel per query and one exogenous query distribution
assumptions: query weights are identical under the compared records
each query channel is record independent
the observed joint law records query identity and post-channel outcome
nonclaims: the global maximum-coefficient bound can be looser than the querywise bound
the result does not cover hidden-record-dependent query scheduling without a new derivation

claims.title: Serial Dobrushin coefficient product bound
claims.scope: a finite serial chain of composable row-stochastic outcome channels
assumptions: adjacent channel output and input alphabets match
every stage is shared by the compared laws
nonclaims: the product is an upper bound and can be strict
serial observation-channel contraction is not a noisy-network coding capacity theorem

claims.title: Predictive equivalence coarsening under shared channels
claims.scope: finite stochastic query-law tensors transformed by one common record-independent channel per query
assumptions: exact equivalence is equality of all pre-channel conditional laws
the transformed family retains the same hidden-record labels and query names
nonclaims: fewer observable classes do not imply fewer microscopic physical states
changing the observation interface is not free exact-world compression

claims.title: Predictive packing and target-cover monotonicity
claims.scope: finite stochastic future-law families before and after shared record-independent outcome channels at one fixed total-variation tolerance
assumptions: packing uses strict pairwise distance greater than twice epsilon
the constructive cover centers are target records from the same family
nonclaims: packing monotonicity supplies a converse rather than an optimal renderer
target-centered cover monotonicity is not an arbitrary-center covering theorem

claims.title: Binary symmetric and erasure channel contraction coefficients
claims.scope: the declared finite binary symmetric and finite-alphabet erasure kernels
assumptions: erasure probability e lies in [0,1] and the erasure symbol is distinct from input outcomes
nonclaims: these kernels are examples and are not asserted to describe all physical measurement noise
the coefficients do not identify a parent simulator implementation

claims.title: Exact rational finite-channel contraction certificate
claims.scope: bounded finite alphabets, exact rational channel rows, and exhaustively enumerated rational probability grids
assumptions: supplied decimals are canonicalized to their finite rational string values
the exhaustive grid denominator and alphabet sizes are the declared bounded test inputs
nonclaims: bounded exhaustive checks are not substitutes for the universal algebraic proof
exact arithmetic for a selected model does not make the empirical model exact
